title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of health claims related to polyphenols in olive and protection of LDL particles from oxidative damage (ID 1333, 1638, 1639, 1696, 2865), maintenance of normal blood HDL cholesterol concentrations (ID 1639), maintenance of normal blood pressure (ID 3781), “anti‐inflammatory properties” (ID 1882), “contributes to the upper respiratory tract health” (ID 3468), “can help to maintain a normal function of gastrointestinal tract” (3779), and “contributes to body defences against external agents” (ID 3467) pursuant to Article 13(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (questions EFSA-Q-2008-2070 and others); adopted on 12 November 2010.
authorConflicts: Declarations of interest of panel members are held by EFSA; not read.
result: A cause and effect relationship is established between consumption of olive oil polyphenols, standardised by their content of hydroxytyrosol and its derivatives, and protection of LDL particles from oxidative damage; proposed wording: 'Consumption of olive oil polyphenols contributes to the protection of blood lipids from oxidative damage'; condition: 5 mg of hydroxytyrosol and its derivatives (e.g. oleuropein complex and tyrosol) in olive oil daily; the concentrations in some olive oils may be too low to supply this amount within a balanced diet. Evidence: dose-dependent decreases in circulating oxidised LDL in one trial of 200 men over 3 weeks (oils with 2.7, 164 and 366 mg/kg phenolic compounds, 25 mL/day; lowest effective dose 5 mg/day) and in smaller trials of 4 days to 3 weeks, one including refined, common and virgin oils with 0 to 150 mg/kg; an acute study of 12 men. Absorption of olive oil phenolics probably exceeds 55-66 mol%; hydroxytyrosol absorption is dose-dependent; tyrosol and hydroxytyrosol are incorporated in lipoprotein fractions; hydroxytyrosol is excreted in urine as glucuronide; hydroxytyrosol monosulfate and homovanillic acid sulphate increased in LDL after high-phenolic oil. In olives, hydroxytyrosol occurs as its elenolic acid ester, oleuropein. Evidence insufficient for maintenance of normal HDL cholesterol; cause and effect not established for normal blood pressure.
